thought.text: While that downloads, let me install Node.js (needed for the `bin/` helper scripts) via NodeSource.

reasoning_content:
While that's downloading, let's install Node.js. Either use the NodeSource setup script (official), or just do apt install nodejs npm (Ubuntu 22.04 has Node 12, and for the ES 7 client and basic scripts it's probably fine). The bin scripts use modern syntax (ES modules). Node 12 supports modules. Let me check what the node scripts in bin require — mainly used for data import, not needed for web app deployment. Actually, to create sample data I can just use curl against the ES API directly. But bin/node_modules exists and suggests that the repo expects node. Let me check whether any of the HTML pages use node... no, they don't. The app is pure browser JS.

Actually, I could create the sample ES index with curl and skip node entirely. But the guide says the software is a web app, and the node scripts in bin/ are auxiliary tools for data import. Installing Node would be useful for the completeness of the toolset, but the core install per the guide is: copy files to the web server + Elasticsearch service.

Let me install Node 18 LTS via NodeSource for a modern runtime (needed for running the bin/ helper scripts, which use ES modules and possibly newer features). I'll do that while the ES download is running.

action.command: curl -sSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_18.x -o /tmp/nodesource_setup.sh && DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive bash /tmp/nodesource_setup.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 && DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y -qq nodejs 2>&1 | tail -2; node --version; npm --version
